title: Delimiting sections with triple backticks or XML markup

videos.script: A prompt reaches the model as one stream of text. Your instructions and the customer's words are the same kind of characters. {{title}} So you mark where the customer's words begin and end. The first mark most people reach for is three backticks. {{backticks}} Then a customer pastes an error message, and errors come wrapped in backticks too. Now the prompt has four sets, and nothing says which pairs with which. Five of six pasted messages fail. {{pasted}} Tags with a name do better. A closing message tag says which section ends, and customers rarely type one. Five of six pass. {{tags}} Rarely is not never. One message closes the tag itself, and the line after it lands among your instructions. {{early}} Escaping the text before it goes in closes that door. The fix lives in the template, where no model has to get it right. {{escape}} By the end of this lesson you can mark what a prompt carries, choose a mark the content cannot contain, and check it by rendering real cases. {{close}}
